scope: Theorem 5.1 (Exact step and comparison) of the manuscript “The canonical massive continuum limit of the two-dimensional O(3) model” (preprints/The-canonical-massive-continuum-limit-of-the-two-dimensional-O3-model-October-4-2026/massive-continuum-o3.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 215 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 e75bfb353c2d3374), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 40. statement: Fix υ > 0 sufficiently small. There are choices of L, the canonical caps and comparison weights, P0, and finally H such that integration against one normalized block observation sends every admitted retained density at b ∈ [Hj/2, 2Hj] to an exact representation of the same form in layer j − 1, with all renewed shape caps. The representation may be iterated when its new coupling belongs to [Hj−1/2, 2Hj−1]; that admission is established separately by shooting in Section 6. Its precise coupling is b′ = b + αh(P) + κh(P) b + ∆, |∆| ≤ CLH−1.05 j . (5.1) Here h is the free history, and the bulk scalar, canonical slots, and kicks use the prescriptions of [28, Equation (5.32)] adapted below to S2. All retained norm caps are renewed. For two regular steps with common geometric scales, let λ = b2 − b1, and let u be the fixed weighted shape discrepancy: canonical coefficient differences, regular-error difference divided by its cap, and covering-gas difference divided by its cap. The regular error difference is measured through order k − 1. Then u′ ≤ qu + CL poly(Hj)ϵh + CL(log Hj)C |λ|/Hj, |λ′ − λ| ≤ CLu + CL poly(Hj)ϵh + CL(log Hj)C |λ|/Hj, q < L−2+υ . (5.2) For identical histories ϵh = 0. If the histories share their last r regular observations, one may take ϵh = (A0/L2)r, with the constant A0 of Section 4. The same-step Lipschitz bounds with no history change hold also for an inclined first step. The representation classes and constants are common to all the admitted histories and periods. Signed covering activities are allowed: the logarithm used in constructing the regular exponent is the convergent connected logarithm of the small background factor, based at one. The mandatory-cover factor is retained as a sum, and no logarithm of the full signed density is taken.
